text:
B: Hi. Hello.
A: Hiya.
B: Er, I'm Adam. Shipley, near Bradford.
A: Joanne. Bolton.
B: Oh, right. Bolton like Bolton Abbey?
A: No, Bolton like Bolton. Nothing to do with it, it's in Yorkshire, isn't it.
B: Yeah, up Wharfedale. Sorry, I just go there a lot. It's a ruined priory, I'm a stonemason, so.
A: You're the stonemason. Elira said.
B: Oh, did she? Yeah, I just had her. She told me about tax codes, actually. Said somebody'd explained them better than her course.
A: That were me. Payroll software, it's my job.
B: Ha. Small world. Is it interesting, payroll?
A: Not really. It's a very old system, councils and NHS use it, and I'm sort of the only one who knows how it actually works. Most of the logic was written before I started, and nobody wrote any of it down. So when it goes wrong at half eleven the night before a pay run, it's me.
B: That's a bit like old buildings, that. Nobody drew anything down, you just open it up and find out what the last bloke did.
A: Yeah. Exactly that. And the last bloke was usually having a bad day.
B: Ha. We get that. You take a block out and there's a bit of brick and a load of cement behind it from nineteen seventy-something. You just think, why.
A: Same. Somebody's put a fix in for one council in 1998 and it's still there, and if you take it out, erm, something in Wigan stops working.
B: Do they not want to replace it?
A: They do. That's the worry.
B: Oh. Right. Sorry.
A: It's fine. What's your dog called? You've not got one, have you.
B: No. My mum and dad had one when I was a kid. You've got a spaniel?
A: Cocker. Bramble. She's in the bins every day. I'll walk her round Moss Bank after this, if it stops raining.
B: Is it raining there?
A: It's Bolton.
B: Ha. Fair. It's grey here an' all. I went up Baildon Moor on Sunday and it was clag the whole way, couldn't see a thing. Still nice, though, sort of, you're just in the cloud on your own.
A: I don't do hills. I tried that running app, Couch to 5K. Twice. Gave up in week three both times.
B: Week three's the hard one, apparently.
A: Is it? That makes me feel better.
B: Er, I don't actually know. I just said it.
A: Ha. Well, I'll take it anyway.
B: Did you do the puzzle bit? I keep asking people, I was rubbish at it.
A: Guessed the shape ones. Didn't see the point.
B: That's what Gary said, I think. Somebody did.
A: Yeah, I had him first. He thinks a barm's a cob.
B: It's a breadcake.
A: Oh, don't you start.
B: Ha, sorry. My mum says breadcake. I'd probably say bap if I'm not thinking.
A: That's worse. Anyway, Mark, my husband, he'd like you, he's always on about old houses. We're in a thirties semi, and he keeps saying he wants to do something with the front, the pebbledash.
B: Oh, don't let him take pebbledash off without looking what's under it. Sometimes it's been put on because the brick's in a bad way. You pull it off and you've got a bigger job than you started with.
A: Right. I'll tell him. He won't listen.
